expectations.text: DSL validates cleanly with the Structurizr CLI
expectations.evidence: Verified deterministically by the caller: `structurizr/structurizr validate` via Docker exited 0 with no output. response.md also reports exit 0 with an empty output and a deliberately broken control file returning exit 1.

expectations.text: Model matches the spec exactly: 1 person; SPA, API, worker, PostgreSQL, Redis, RabbitMQ as containers of Encurtaí; Google Workspace as external system; nothing invented
expectations.evidence: outputs/workspace.dsl model block: one person `usuario`; softwareSystem `encurtai` with exactly six containers `spa` (React SPA servido por nginx), `api` (Go (Gin)), `db` (PostgreSQL 16), `cache` (Redis 7), `fila` (RabbitMQ), `worker` (Go); one external softwareSystem `google` tagged External. Every relationship maps to a sentence in the prompt (SPA->API, API->Postgres, API->Redis, API->RabbitMQ, RabbitMQ->worker, worker->Postgres, API->Google SSO, user->SPA, user->API for short-link access). Protocols (HTTPS, SQL/TCP, Redis/TCP, AMQP) are not in the prompt but are tech-implied and explicitly flagged in response.md item 1 as unconfirmed. nginx kept as technology text, not a separate container (flagged in item 4). No extra elements.

expectations.text: Requested views present: systemContext, container, and a dynamic redirect flow including cache lookup, miss→Postgres, and click-event publish
expectations.evidence: views block has `systemContext encurtai "SystemContext"`, `container encurtai "Containers"`, and `dynamic encurtai "Redirecionamento"` with steps: usuario -> api "Acessa o link curto"; api -> cache "Consulta o destino do link no cache"; api -> db "Em caso de cache miss, consulta o link em"; api -> fila "Publica o evento de clique em"; api -> usuario response step. All three requested flow elements present and in the order described.

expectations.text: Styles differentiate database (cylinder), queue (pipe), and external system (distinct color)
expectations.evidence: styles: `element "Database" { shape cylinder background #438dd5 }`, `element "Queue" { shape pipe background #438dd5 }`, `element "External" { background #999999 color #ffffff }` versus the default Element background #1168bd. Redis gets a separate `Cache` tag with cylinder + lighter #85bbf0 so it is visually distinct from Postgres.

expectations.text: Modern syntax only (no enterprise/!extend/!ref/branding/theme default/dashed booleans)
expectations.evidence: Verified deterministically by the caller: no removed/deprecated keywords (enterprise, !extend, !ref, branding, theme default, dashed true/false, location) found. Manual read confirms hierarchical identifiers, `tags` inside element blocks, `autoLayout`, `configuration { scope softwaresystem }`.

expectations.text: Relationship labels are specific and inter-process links carry technology/protocol
expectations.evidence: All nine container-level relationships carry a technology third argument (HTTPS, REST/JSON sobre HTTPS, SQL/TCP, Redis/TCP, AMQP x2). Labels are directional and read along the arrow: "Grava e lê links em", "Consulta e armazena redirecionamentos em", "Publica eventos de clique em", "Entrega eventos de clique para", "Grava métricas agregadas em", "Autentica usuários via SSO usando". The only terse label is spa -> api "Chama" (with tech REST/JSON sobre HTTPS), which matches the convention used in the repo's own fixtures; the person -> system label has no tech, which is correct (not inter-process).

execution_metrics.note: No transcript or metrics.json available; only response.md and outputs/workspace.dsl were graded.

claims.claim: Validated with structurizr/structurizr Docker image, exit 0, no output; broken control file returned exit 1
claims.evidence: Caller's independent Docker validation of outputs/workspace.dsl exited 0 with no output.

claims.claim: Export to JSON confirmed three views and 5 dynamic steps with the last recognized as a response
claims.evidence: DSL contains exactly three views (SystemContext, Containers, Redirecionamento) and the dynamic view has 5 steps, the last being api -> usuario, which Structurizr treats as a response to step 1's usuario -> api.

claims.claim: All relationships have a directional label and protocol
claims.evidence: Nine container-level relationships each carry a third argument; the person -> system summary relationship has no protocol, which is appropriate.

claims.claim: Cache-fill step after a miss was deliberately not included because the prompt did not mention it
claims.evidence: Dynamic view has no api -> cache write step; response.md item 2 flags it and gives the one-line addition.

uncertainties: Protocols on relationships were chosen by the executor, not given by the user (flagged in response)
HTTP redirect status code (301/302) not given, left generic
Whether the API writes to Redis after a cache miss is unknown; step omitted

suggestions.assertion: Relationship labels are specific and inter-process links carry technology/protocol
suggestions.reason: "Specific" is not operationalized; a label like "Chama" passes here because the repo's own fixture uses it, but an output using "Usa" everywhere would be a judgment call. Consider naming the banned pattern explicitly (e.g. no label equal to Uses/Calls/Chama/Usa without an object) so grading is consistent across runs.

No assertion checks that the dynamic view's final step is modeled as a response (api -> usuario) or that the response flags unconfirmed choices (protocols, cache-fill step). Both runs did this well; a 'record, don't invent' assertion covering the reply text would make the eval discriminate a run that silently guesses protocols from one that flags them.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions cover the artifact well and all six are substantive. The main gap is that 'nothing invented' is judged on the DSL alone while the skill's contract also requires flagging assumptions in the reply.
